options: Defines 2 axes and 2 planes of reference
Relates to a well-defined position of the human body
Was adopted by an international agreement in Paris
questions.explanation: The NA is an international Latin nomenclature (adopted in Paris, 1955) referring to the reference anatomical position, with 3 axes, 3 planes and dynamic reference points.

questions.stem: In the reference anatomical position, the subject is:
options: With the legs extended and the feet together on the ground
Upright, with the upper limbs hanging along the trunk
With the gaze straight and horizontal
A living human body, lying supine
questions.explanation: Reference position: living, upright body, upper limbs hanging along the trunk, palms facing forward, gaze straight and horizontal, legs extended, feet together on the ground.

questions.stem: An anatomy drawing shows a subject standing with the palms facing the thighs (thumbs forward). Compared with the reference anatomical position, what is wrong?
options: The gaze should be directed upward
The upper limbs should be raised horizontally
Nothing, palms facing medially is the reference position
The subject should be lying down
questions.explanation: In the reference position the palms face forward (anteriorly). Palms facing inward is a classic exam distractor.

options: The body axis is a vertical line dropped from the top of the skull (vertex)
The axis of the foot passes through the 3rd toe
The axis of the hand passes through the 3rd finger
The axis of the hand is a transverse axis
The body axis passes through the centre of gravity, located at the level of the pelvis
questions.explanation: The hand axis is longitudinal through the 3rd finger; the foot axis is longitudinal through the 2nd toe, not the 3rd.

questions.stem: Through which digit does the reference axis of the foot pass?
questions.explanation: The foot axis is the longitudinal axis passing through the 2nd toe (the hand axis passes through the 3rd finger).

options: Is the plane in which abduction and adduction take place
Divides the body into anterior and posterior parts
Is a vertical plane parallel to the forehead
Divides the body into right and left parts
questions.explanation: The frontal plane is vertical, parallel to the forehead, and separates anterior from posterior; abduction/adduction occur in it around a sagittal axis. Right/left = median sagittal plane; parallel to the ground = transverse plane.

options: Divides the body into two symmetrical parts, right and left
Divides the body into medial and lateral parts
questions.explanation: The median sagittal plane passes through the midline giving symmetrical right and left halves. Medial/lateral (asymmetrical) parts are produced by a paramedian sagittal plane.

questions.stem: The transverse plane is also called:
questions.explanation: The transverse plane is the horizontal or axial plane, parallel to the ground, dividing the body into superior (cranial) and inferior (caudal) parts. Coronal = frontal plane.
Flexion (forward) and extension (backward) occur around a transverse axis in a sagittal plane.

options: Moves a part of the body away from the median plane
Is performed in a frontal plane
Is performed in a transverse plane
Is performed around a sagittal axis
Brings a part of the body closer to the median plane
questions.explanation: Abduction moves a segment away from the median plane (adduction brings it closer); both occur around a sagittal axis in a frontal plane.

options: A rotary movement from inside to outside
A rotary movement from outside to inside
questions.explanation: Lateral rotation goes from inside to outside (medial rotation from outside to inside); rotations occur around a vertical axis in a transverse plane.

options: Medial means near the median sagittal plane
Internal means close to the surface
Caudal is a synonym of inferior
Ipsilateral means belonging to two different sides
Proximal means close to the root of the limb
questions.explanation: Ipsilateral = same side (contralateral = different sides). Internal = facing the inside of a cavity or organ; close to the surface is superficial.

questions.stem: Which of the following terms are synonyms of "superior"?
questions.explanation: Superior = cranial = cephalic (near the upper end). Caudal = inferior; dorsal = posterior; proximal = close to the root of a limb.

questions.stem: About the levels of structural organization of the human body:
options: The cell is the basic structural and functional unit
An organ brings together different tissues for a specific function, e.g. liver
A system is a set of dissimilar organs participating in the same function
A tissue is a group of cells playing a homologous role, e.g. bone tissue
An apparatus is a set of structurally comparable organs, e.g. the skeletal system
questions.explanation: The definitions are inverted in the last two: a system groups structurally similar organs (skeletal system, CNS), while an apparatus groups dissimilar organs for one function (digestive, circulatory).

questions.stem: Which of the following belong to the apparatuses of relational life?
questions.explanation: Relational life: locomotor (skeletal, articular, muscular systems), nervous and sensory apparatus. Circulatory and endocrine belong to the nutrition apparatuses.
The locomotor apparatus groups the skeletal, articular and muscular systems; the peripheral nervous system belongs to the nervous apparatus.

questions.stem: About the topographical organization of the human body:
options: The neck is a passageway for visceral, vascular and nervous elements
The head contains the initial segments of the digestive and respiratory systems
The limbs are formed essentially by viscera
The trunk contains the thoracic cavity above and the abdominopelvic cavity below
The shape of the body is determined by the osteo-cartilaginous skeleton
questions.explanation: The limbs are extensions of the trunk formed by bones, joints, muscles, vessels and nerves, not viscera.

questions.stem: The image shows three sections of the head (1, 2, 3 from left to right). In which planes were they cut?
questions.explanation: Section 1 shows both hemispheres from the front (frontal plane), section 2 cuts the head into right/left halves through the midline (median sagittal), and section 3 is parallel to the ground through the eyes (transverse/axial).
